clue.text: Projection for attaching rope is holding male climber

indicators.note: holding means the cleat grips the male letter inside itself

parts.note: a cleat is a projecting fitting to which a rope is made fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber's rope fitting is clutching a man on the rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer with a rope, but it is the garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a familiar climbing plant trained up walls and trellises.

clue.text: A lord one recollected as Renaissance man

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected, gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman reminisces as a man of many talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but as re-collected it shuffles A LORD ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci is the archetypal polymath of the Italian Renaissance.

clue.text: Small bit of wood that remains after starting fire

indicators.note: after places the word for remains behind the fire-starter

parts.note: a match is what you strike when starting a fire
to stick is to remain or stay put

explanation.surface: The charred sliver left over once you've lit the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a spent match, but it splits into definition plus a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is a slender piece of wood, the stem of a match.

clue.text: Beat time by a runner, or equivalent

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a mount is a horse, a runner in a race

explanation.surface: Thrash the clock with an athlete, or match it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a horse (MOUNT) running in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount means equal in effect or value.

clue.text: Like a spell of good weather, reportedly brief

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.words: Like a spell of good weather
parts.note: summery means characteristic of fine summer weather

explanation.surface: A forecast of a sunny spell, said to be short.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary account is brief and given without detail.

clue.text: Greek god in part of Middle East set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Suez is a city and canal zone in Egypt, often counted in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A Greek deity installed in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is king of the Olympian gods in Greek myth.

clue.text: Weapon from gunshop I stole

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gun I took from a weapons shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a handgun, a firearm.

clue.text: Purchase residue from cheese-making, say, in passing

indicators.note: say signals that what precedes is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: buy (purchase) the whey (the liquid left after curdling milk for cheese)

explanation.surface: Picking up the leftovers from a dairy's cheese production.
explanation.walkthrough: Whey is the watery liquid left when curds form in cheese-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Said by the way, a remark is made incidentally, in passing.

clue.text: In nervous way? Hardly so, you might think

definitions.meaning: read as UN- plus a word meaning with ease, so 'not with ease', i.e. hardly

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as a prefix meaning not plus an adverb meaning with ease, giving a jokey sense of 'hardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasily describes acting with anxiety or discomfort, a nervous manner.

clue.text: Like an attachment to machine in Northern town

definitions.meaning: a part that is bolted on to a machine, an add-on
a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England

explanation.walkthrough: BOLTON is a large town near Manchester in northern England; split as two words it describes an add-on part.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a Lancashire mill town; as 'bolt-on' it means an attached accessory.

clue.text: Control device which, say, comes on daily

indicators.note: in an across clue, X comes on Y means X is placed after Y

parts.note: The Times is a daily newspaper

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: which sounds the same as a sorceress

explanation.surface: A gadget that switches itself on every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an innocent description of the device, hiding that 'daily' names a newspaper and 'which, say' is a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A time switch is an automatic timer that controls when an appliance turns on or off.

clue.text: Dagger seen as knight turned on king

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: turned means the title for a knight is read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A dagger appears when a knight rounds on his king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses the knight's title, and 'on' sets it after the king in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Reason to expect the worst, making potato salad

parts.note: murphy is an informal word for a potato, from Irish associations
slaw is short for coleslaw, a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: Something is bound to go wrong when you make potato salad.
explanation.walkthrough: MURPHY is slang for a potato; SLAW (coleslaw) is a shredded cabbage salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy's law is the adage that anything which can go wrong will go wrong.

clue.text: Part of school outstanding, doing homework well?

parts.note: British schools divide pupils into houses for competitions
proud means standing out from a surface, projecting

explanation.surface: A school house excels at its homework.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE is a division of a British school; 'homework' means housework, not school prep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone house-proud keeps their home immaculate, a witty take on doing housework well.

clue.text: For whom dismantling state is par?

definitions.text: For whom dismantling state is par?

indicators.note: dismantling means the letters are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone for whom breaking up a nation is normal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'dismantling' rearranges STATE IS PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A separatist wants a region to break away from the state, for whom splitting it is the norm.

clue.text: After arrest, promises to pay in full

definitions.note: adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning abundant

indicators.note: after places the promises following the arrest

parts.note: to cop is slang for to arrest or catch
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Once arrested, someone vows to settle the debt completely.
explanation.walkthrough: IOUs are notes promising to pay ('I owe you'); 'After' keeps them behind COP.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, supplied in full measure.

clue.text: Under cape, am I only in underwear?

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the following letters come below

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
taken as written
sole means only, single

explanation.surface: Am I wearing nothing but undies beneath my cloak?
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's loose sleeveless undergarment.

clue.text: Form of market domination, as might be expected, restricting work to ring

indicators.note: restricting means the first word confines the others within it

parts.note: duly means in the proper or expected way
OP is short for opus, a work
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A monopoly-style arrangement that confines work to a cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' just links the two inserted pieces. 'Ring' suggests a price-fixing ring, but it is only a letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A duopoly is a market controlled by just two suppliers.

clue.text: Awfully brittle old book

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: An extremely fragile antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the book, or text, of an opera.

clue.text: Expresses opposition in articles

explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest; objects are physical things or articles.

clue.text: Notice English food, like hot cakes, especially

parts.note: to mark is to notice or observe
table can mean the food served at a meal, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: Spot some English fare, particularly hot cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that 'sell like hot cakes' are very saleable, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that sell like hot cakes are eminently saleable, the idiom pointing to easy selling.

clue.text: Very eager, as artist, to join band

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A keen painter joins a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very keen.

clue.text: Scrape back of Blarney stone

parts.note: to rub is to scrape or chafe

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Kissing the Blarney Stone means rubbing the back of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blarney Stone, kissed for eloquence, is the false lead; 'stone' means a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious stone, a gem.

clue.text: Electoral official falsifying returns, i.e. putting Conservative in

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is put inside the jumble
falsifying means the letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation spelt without stops

explanation.surface: An election official rigs the returns by slipping a Tory in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsifying' rearranges RETURNS and IE; 'putting ... in' inserts C into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer examines votes at an election to ensure fairness.

clue.text: Run slowly, in vain

definitions.meaning: an engine ticking over without load

explanation.definitionFit: An engine can idle; idle also means useless or futile.

clue.text: After operation, I swallowed painkiller

indicators.note: after places what follows behind the operation

parts.note: ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: Post-surgery, a patient gulped down a pain reliever.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, used to relieve pain.

clue.text: Look inside narrow window to see queen's lover

indicators.note: inside means the look word goes into the window word

parts.note: a lancet is a tall, narrow pointed window
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Peer through a slit window to spy on the queen's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot was Queen Guinevere's lover in Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend Sir Lancelot is Guinevere's lover.

clue.text: Revolting behaviour depicted in second issue

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication

explanation.surface: Disgusting conduct shown in a second printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' suggests disgusting, but it means rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct inciting rebellion against authority.
